title: The Ransom Rows of Barrowfen
story: Barrowfen the Reed Marshal has penned the village's geese in his marsh, arranging his mud-soldiers in neat rows to guard them. He offers a deal: pay one silver coin per soldier, and the geese go free. Mr 6 counts the ranks instead of charging them.
question: Barrowfen's soldiers stand in 14 rows of 9. The villagers have already gathered 87 silver coins. How many more coins do they still need to pay one coin per soldier?
hint: First figure out how many soldiers there are altogether, then compare with the 87 coins already collected.
victory: The villagers found the last 39 coins under the church steps, and Barrowfen — who had honestly expected a fight — released every goose with a soggy bow. 'Counting,' said Mr 6, 'is cheaper than clanging.'
imagePrompt: Rows of squat mud-soldiers standing in a misty reed marsh guarding a flock of honking geese, with a small caped numeral 6 tallying them on a slate.
solution: Count the soldiers: 14 rows × 9 = 126 soldiers, so 126 coins are needed.
praise: Multiplying rows by soldiers was the perfect first move — the missing step was subtracting the 87 coins already collected.
